security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU's IOMMU emulation defines IOHGATP_Sv32x4 as 1 (the old hgatp-style value) instead of 8, OR uses MODE=8 exclusively for Sv39x4 without checking fctl.GXL to disambiguate between Sv32x4 (GXL=1) and Sv39x4 (GXL=0)
security_spec.summary: IOMMU iohgatp.MODE uses shared encoding 8 for both Sv32x4 and Sv39x4, disambiguated by fctl.GXL; stale value 1 for Sv32x4 or missing GXL check causes G-stage walks to misinterpret page table format, leading to wrong SPA translations for DMA

findings.finding: Line 786 compares fsc_mode against RISCV_IOMMU_CAP_SV32 (BIT_ULL(8)=256) instead of RISCV_IOMMU_DC_FSC_IOSATP_MODE_SV32 (=8). The condition 'fsc_mode == RISCV_IOMMU_CAP_SV32' is always false, making the SXL=1 first-stage SV32 capability check dead code. Any fsc_mode value (including unsupported modes) passes validation when SXL=1. The validate_process_ctx() function (line 853) correctly uses RISCV_IOMMU_DC_FSC_IOSATP_MODE_SV32 for the same check.

spec_citations.excerpt: Sv32 vs Sv39 mode (both MODE=8) disambiguated by hardware XLEN (GXL/SXL field). Hardware must validate supported modes against capabilities register.

findings.finding: validate_device_ctx() validates only BARE-mode interactions with T2GPA and MSIPTP but does NOT validate whether the G-stage (IOHGATP) mode value (8/9/10) is supported by s->cap hardware capabilities or within valid range. By contrast, first-stage (FSC) mode validation is performed at lines 759-808. G-stage mode validation is deferred to the actual page-table walk in riscv_iommu_spa_fetch() and pdt_memory_read(), which catch unsupported modes only at translation time rather than at context-fetch time. A malicious guest could install an unsupported G-stage mode in a device context, which would be silently cached and only rejected on access.

The G-stage (pass=1) MODE=8 disambiguation correctly uses s->fctl & RISCV_IOMMU_FCTL_GXL: when GXL=1 selects Sv32X4 (32-bit, levels=2/ptesize=4), when GXL=0 selects Sv39X4 (64-bit, levels=3/ptesize=8). This correctly disambiguates Sv32x4 vs Sv39x4 which share the IOHGATP MODE encoding value 8.

IOHGATP mode enum correctly defines Sv32x4=8 (not the old hgatp-style value 1). Sv32x4 and Sv39x4 both map to MODE=8 per RISC-V IOMMU spec, requiring GXL-based disambiguation in the page-table walkers. The Sv48x4=9 and Sv57x4=10 values are also correct.
